For this project, the team considered a number of corridors/local road networks that represented different levels of crime and crash exposures. • Data collection effort. Data collection required members of the project team to drive each roadway (ideally multiple times to increase data point density) at night to collect lighting data with the Roadway Lighting Mobile Measurement System (RLMMS). Due to time and budget limitations, the project team could only take measurements for a limited mileage of roadways. After carefully weighing the aforementioned factors, the project team decided to select major roadway corridors based on the MassDOT HPMS data and local roads based on census block groups. The former includes all Massachusetts state-maintained roadways classified in Cambridge falling in the functional classes of principal arterials, minor arterials, and collectors. Because the local roadways are a much denser network, it was not feasible to select such roads by segment. Figure 20 shows the final roadways selected for lighting measurement. The red lines represent the selected major roadway segments, and the light green areas are block groups within which local roadways will be measured.
